title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Water-sector PLC attacks now reported in at least 12 states as exposure, not malware, stays the story
items.content_text: The campaign against internet-facing water controllers that began around 27 July has now been reported in at least 12 states, including Minnesota, Michigan, Georgia, New Jersey, South Dakota and Alabama. The FBI and EPA public-service alert of 30 July confirms actors reached exposed Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 PLCs, changed IP addresses and passwords to lock operators out of monitoring and control, and in at least one case modified controller logic. Reported physical effects include loss of pressure and localized flooding; in Georgia, Clayton County Water Authority — serving roughly 300,000 customers — issued a boil-water advisory after a pressure drop. Two weeks on, no new intrusions have been disclosed, but the condition that enabled all of this — controllers reachable from the internet with weak or shared credentials — is unchanged. Attribution to Iran remains suspected, not confirmed.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: FBI/EPA public-service alert; The Record, Axios, CBS News — FBI-confirmed disruption, attribution pending
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attacks from 27 Jul 2026; FBI/EPA alert 30 Jul; 12-state tally reported 4 Aug 2026

items.title: More than 4,400 Rockwell PLCs are reachable from the internet — 22 sat in the cities that were hit
items.content_text: A Shodan query run on 3 August returned 4,407 devices exposing EtherNet/IP port 44818, with roughly 65% in the United States, 12% in Canada and 3% in Spain. Of the 22 controllers located in cities where water utilities reported incidents, 19 were running firmware susceptible to CVE-2017-16740, a Modbus TCP buffer overflow affecting MicroLogix 1400 Series B and C on firmware 21.002 and earlier; Rockwell fixed it in revision 21.003. For a water operator the finding is uncomfortable but useful: the exposed population is a countable list, most of the affected firmware is a decade behind, and the same scan you can run against your own public IP ranges will tell you whether you are on it.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs analysis; The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Shodan scan data 3 Aug 2026 — reported week of 3–7 Aug 2026

items.title: Federal advisory adds Schneider and Siemens PLCs to the Iran-affiliated targeting list (AA26-097A, updated 22 Jul)
items.content_text: The mechanism behind the water disruptions is documented in joint advisory AA26-097A, updated on 22 July. Federal agencies say Iran-affiliated actors are connecting to internet-exposed controllers using the vendors’ own engineering software — Rockwell Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Schneider EcoStruxure Control Expert and Siemens TIA Portal — over ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502 and 22, then extracting, modifying and deleting project logic. In one US case the FBI found a downloaded project file that kept ladder logic for downstream function but added logic overriding the instruction sets that held safe operating parameters, and disabled shutdown and alarm logic so equipment could drift into unsafe states without alerting operators. The update newly names Schneider Modicon M340 (BMX P34) and Siemens S7-1200 alongside Rockwell CompactLogix and Micro850.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Updated 22 Jul 2026 (originally published 7 Apr 2026) — campaign ongoing

items.title: CISA #StopRansomware advisory on Gunra: affiliates are getting in through exposed VPNs and firewalls
items.content_text: Six agencies — CISA, the FBI, DC3, NSA, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency — published joint advisory AA26-222A on 10 August covering Gunra ransomware. Gunra emerged in April 2025 from leaked Conti source code and has since grown into a ransomware-as-a-service operation with recruited affiliates. The advisory says affiliates breach networks through exposed edge infrastructure — VPN gateways, firewall appliances and RDP-reachable systems — then exfiltrate before encrypting. Named victim sectors include utilities, government and transport. For a water system the relevant read is that the same under-patched remote-access box that would let an operator in from home is the documented entry point, and that a billing or SCADA-historian outage can force manual operation just as effectively as a controller attack.

items.title: Dragos: 1,140 industrial ransomware incidents in Q2, and none of them touched a control system directly
items.content_text: Dragos’ Q2 2026 analysis, published 11 August, counted 1,140 ransomware incidents at industrial organizations, up 12% from 1,020 in Q1. North America accounted for 514 and Europe 316. The finding that matters most to a utility is negative: Dragos observed no case in the quarter where a ransomware operator directly manipulated an industrial control system. Operations were disrupted anyway, through IT, ERP and virtualization layers that industrial processes depend on. For water and wastewater that reframes the planning question — the realistic ransomware scenario is not encrypted PLCs but a dead historian, an unavailable billing and work-order system, and a SCADA server that will not boot because its hypervisor is encrypted.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis Q2 2026; Help Net Security

items.title: CVSS 10 command injection in Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway — water and wastewater named (ICSA-26-225-02)
items.content_text: CISA released 14 ICS advisories on 13 August, led by a maximum-severity flaw in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway. CVE-2026-19188 carries a CVSS score of 10.0: the gateway’s ‘Net Check’ feature passes user-supplied input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system without sanitizing it, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary OS commands as root with no user interaction. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected. CISA lists energy, critical manufacturing and water and wastewater among the deployment sectors. These combined HMI/gateway/DTU units are exactly the kind of low-cost remote-monitoring box that ends up on a lift station or booster pump with a cellular connection and no firewall in front of it — the same profile as the controllers hit in the current campaign.

items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA/FTD zero-day added to CISA KEV after exploitation for denial of service
items.content_text: CISA added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August, including CVE-2026-20349, a heap-inspection flaw in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Firewall Threat Defense that Cisco patched after it was exploited as a zero-day for denial-of-service attacks. The other two are a use-after-free in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (CVE-2026-68820) and a SQL injection flaw in Metabase (CVE-2026-72898). ASA and FTD appliances are common as the boundary device between a utility’s business network and its SCADA network and as the VPN concentrator operators use after hours; a DoS on that box does not breach the plant but it can take remote monitoring and vendor support offline exactly when they are needed.

items.title: August ICS Patch Tuesday: maximum-severity authentication bypass in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050
items.content_text: Siemens published 10 advisories on 11 August, headlined by a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices (SSA-834709) that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with elevated privileges. Siemens also fixed a critical code-execution flaw in Siveillance Video Management Servers and high-severity issues in Solid Edge, Simcenter Nastran, the Siemens License Server, Simcenter Femap, Parasolid and Logo! Soft Comfort. Schneider Electric issued two advisories covering NetBotz 5 and PowerChute Serial Shutdown, and Phoenix Contact one for multiple PLCnext firmware flaws exploitable without authentication for DoS or SQL injection. Water utilities most often meet this list through NetBotz environmental monitoring in plant rooms and PowerChute on UPS-backed SCADA servers.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact PSIRT via SecurityWeek

items.title: AVEVA Enterprise SCADA and Hitachi Energy APM Edge among the 13 August CISA advisory batch
items.content_text: Alongside the Haiwell gateway flaw, CISA’s 13 August release included ICSA-26-225-01 covering AVEVA Enterprise SCADA at CVSS 7.1, ICSA-26-225-04 for Hitachi Energy APM Edge at CVSS 8.8 in the energy sector, ICSA-26-225-05 for hard-coded credentials in ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 at CVSS 8.1, and ICSA-26-225-14 for Johnson Controls Metasys versions 12–15, where low-privilege users can inject persistent payloads via crafted URLs. None is reported as exploited. AVEVA Enterprise SCADA is the item most likely to be in a mid-size water utility’s control room, and Metasys often runs the same campus as a treatment plant’s building systems — a reminder that the facility-management network frequently shares infrastructure with process control.

items.title: Water Cyber Shield Act would give EPA enforcement teeth and $300M a year; Water Watch Center targets the smallest systems
items.content_text: Senators Adam Schiff and Amy Klobuchar introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act on 11 August. The bill would grant EPA explicit authority to conduct cybersecurity assessments, enforce corrective measures and set security standards with CISA and NIST; authorize $300 million annually through the Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds; mandate risk assessments for large systems; extend mandatory incident reporting to state- and locally-owned facilities; and shield sensitive utility data from public disclosure. Separately, DEF CON Franklin and the National Rural Water Association launched the Water Watch Center, offering managed detection and response through five security firms to utilities serving fewer than 10,000 people — 91% of the roughly 50,000 US community water systems. It builds on a two-year pilot that paired nearly 450 volunteers with utilities in seven states.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Senate bill summary via SecurityWeek; DEF CON Franklin / NRWA announcement

items.title: EPA publishes a state-facing checklist for proactively strengthening drinking water systems
items.content_text: On 13 August EPA issued a new checklist intended to help state primacy agencies work through drinking-water system resilience before an incident rather than after one. It arrives the same week Mississippi’s Department of Health advised its public water systems following the national attack campaign, and it sits alongside EPA’s existing cybersecurity incident-response plan template, procurement checklist and incident action checklists. For an individual utility the practical value is anticipatory: the questions a state asks during a sanitary survey tend to follow the checklist the state was handed, so reading it now is a preview of what your primacy agency will want evidence for.
